dedupe_keys.name: mic aggregation and estimate of internet traffic in japan broadband subscriber traffic twice yearly

description: Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications publishes twice a year its aggregation and estimate of internet traffic in Japan, with figures as of May and November of each year; releases are listed on the ministry's telecom competition policy portal from 2009 to the latest, for May 2026. The series is compiled with the cooperation of internet service providers and internet exchanges and estimates the total download and upload traffic of broadband subscribers in Japan, and the ministry's statistics database offers the aggregated values as an Excel workbook together with a summary PDF, alongside a separate series on the current state of mobile communications traffic and the annual voice traffic statistics. Coverage: Japan. Format and access: press releases and PDF summaries on the ministry's website, with aggregated values as XLSX, free. Caveats: estimates scaled from a sample of cooperating ISPs to the national total; the method and the ISP panel may change between releases, and the details of the method and the cooperating organisations were not read in this session. Simulation uses: long-term growth and peak of national broadband traffic for capacity planning, and baselines for detecting traffic shifts after disasters such as the 2011 earthquake. Related records: the JPIX traffic graphs give exchange-level traffic, the MIC telecom statistics database gives subscriptions, and the case study on 2011 earthquake traffic routing describes a disruption.
